chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the selling of the parchments (copies of the Holy Quran) and buying them, so he said: 'Do not buy the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but buy the iron (ink pigment), and the paper, and the two covers, and say, "I am buying this from you for such and such (an amount)."'

key_terms.الدَّفَّتَيْنِ: The two covers, referring to the front and back covers of the book
key_terms.الْحَدِيدَ: Iron, referring to iron gall ink used for ink pigment
key_terms.الْمَصَاحِفِ: Plural of Mushaf, referring to copies of the Holy Quran
key_terms.الْوَرَقَ: Paper, the material on which the Quran is written

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to buy and sell copies of the Quran according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between the Quran as a divine revelation and the physical manuscript as a commodity, preventing the commodification of the Word of God. By instructing the buyer to purchase materials like paper and ink while explicitly stating the intent, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a method to preserve the spiritual sanctity of the Mushaf during commercial transactions. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the sacred text itself and its tangible载体, ensuring reverence is maintained in everyday economic dealings.
